question: Pipe P can fill (2)/(5) part of a tank in 42 hours and pipe Q can fill (2)/(5) part of the same tank in 30 hours. Both P and Q were kept open for 5 hours, then both were closed. Pipe R alone was then opened and it emptied the water in the tank in 12 hours. Pipes P, Q and R together can fill the empty tank in:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time for P = 42 × 5/2 = 105 hrs, Time for Q = 30 × 5/2 = 75 hrs.

Let Capacity = 525 units (LCM of 105, 75). Efficiency: P = 5, Q = 7.

Work done by P + Q in 5 hours = (5 + 7) × 5 = 60 units.

Efficiency of R (emptying) = 60 / 12 = 5 units/hr.

Net efficiency of P + Q + R = 5 + 7 − 5 = 7 units/hr.

Total time required = 525 / 7 = 75 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 75 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: P fills 2/5 tank in 42 hrs, Q fills 2/5 tank in 30 hrs. R empties filled water in 12 hrs.

Formula: Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

⇒ Time for P to fill full tank = 42 × 5 ÷ 2 = 105 hours

⇒ Time for Q to fill full tank = 30 × 5 ÷ 2 = 75 hours

⇒ Let Total capacity of tank = LCM(105, 75) = 525 units

⇒ Efficiency of P + Q = 5 + 7 = 12 units/hr

⇒ Water filled in 5 hours = 12 × 5 = 60 units

⇒ R empties 60 units in 12 hours

⇒ Efficiency of R = −(60 ÷ 12) = −5 units/hr

⇒ Combined efficiency of P, Q, and R = 5 + 7 − 5 = 7 units/hr

⇒ Time to fill the tank together = Total Quantity ÷ Total Efficiency

⇒ Time = 525 ÷ 7 = 75 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 75 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

Inlet pipes fill the tank (positive efficiency) while outlet pipes empty the tank (negative efficiency).

Time and Efficiency Relation

Time taken to fill/empty is inversely proportional to efficiency: Time = Capacity ÷ Efficiency.

Pipes and Cisterns Net Work

If pipe A fills in x hours and pipe B empties in y hours, net work in 1 hour = (1/x − 1/y).
